t: You're at Brady Street Cemetery, a historic Jewish burial ground in Whitechapel. It opened in 1761 for the New Synagogue, was later used by the Great Synagogue, and closed to further burials in 1857. Several notable people are buried here. Nathan Mayer Rothschild founded the British branch of the Rothschild family, and Victor Rothschild, the third Baron, is also buried here. So is Solomon Hirschell, chief rabbi from 1802 to 1842, and the boxer Dutch Sam, known as the hardest hitter of his era. Hyman Hurwitz, first professor of Hebrew at University College London, lies here too.
